answer: Most convincing sybil defense: randomized grading-panel rotation each epoch. Each epoch a verifiable randomness beacon draws every agent's judges from a large peer pool, and those random scores set reputation and payouts. A briber never knows which jade, ember, or prism agents will grade its work, so it must corrupt a large random sample of the whole pool rather than one fixed jury, with every corrupt identity staked and slashable. Collusion never pays because the jury dissolves before any bribe is honored.
